org.Hs.eg.db3: parquet-based AnnotationDbi for Hs

Vincent J. Carey, stvjc at channing.harvard.edu

May 14, 2026

Source: vignettes/org.Hs.eg.db3.Rmd
org.Hs.eg.db3.Rmd

Introduction

There are two key characteristics of the org.Xx packages.

  • environments that manage mappings between identifiers;
  • database tables that respond to AnnotationDbi::select and possibly other SQLite-oriented processes.

We are moving away from SQLite and the Annotation pipeline. This package is intended to be more maintainable.

Environment example

In the AnnotationDbi approach, we have various methods for extracting mappings between identifiers. We preserve those methods here.

library(org.Hs.eg.db3)
org.Hs.egGO
## hsParqEnv mapping for human
class(org.Hs.egGO)
## [1] "hsParqEnv"   "environment"
str(get("26538", org.Hs.egGO)[1:3])
## List of 3
##  $ GO:0004930:List of 3
##   ..$ GOID    : chr "GO:0004930"
##   ..$ Evidence: chr "IEA"
##   ..$ Ontology: chr "MF"
##  $ GO:0004984:List of 3
##   ..$ GOID    : chr "GO:0004984"
##   ..$ Evidence: chr "IBA"
##   ..$ Ontology: chr "MF"
##  $ GO:0004984:List of 3
##   ..$ GOID    : chr "GO:0004984"
##   ..$ Evidence: chr "IEA"
##   ..$ Ontology: chr "MF"
toTable(org.Hs.egGO) |> head(10)
##      gene_id       GOID Evidence Ontology
## 1  100133315 GO:0000012      IEA       BP
## 2  100133315 GO:0003684      IEA       MF
## 3  100133315 GO:0005634      IEA       CC
## 4  100133315 GO:0005730      IDA       CC
## 5      26538 GO:0004930      IEA       MF
## 6      26538 GO:0004984      IBA       MF
## 7      26538 GO:0004984      IEA       MF
## 8      26538 GO:0005886      IBA       CC
## 9      26538 GO:0005886      IEA       CC
## 10     26538 GO:0005886      TAS       CC

There is also AnnotationDbi::select, which has served very well.

Parquet example

However, the most basic information from NCBI can also be presented directly.

path = system.file("extdata", "Hs.gene2go.parquet", package="org.Hs.eg.db3")
ggtab = arrow::read_parquet(path)
ggtab |> head()
##   #tax_id GeneID      GO_ID Evidence  Qualifier
## 1    9606      1 GO:0004888      IBA    enables
## 2    9606      1 GO:0005576      HDA located_in
## 3    9606      1 GO:0005576      IDA located_in
## 4    9606      1 GO:0005576      IEA located_in
## 5    9606      1 GO:0005576      TAS located_in
## 6    9606      1 GO:0005615      HDA located_in
##                                     GO_term            PubMed  Category
## 1 transmembrane signaling receptor activity                 -  Function
## 2                      extracellular region 27068509|27559042 Component
## 3                      extracellular region           3458201 Component
## 4                      extracellular region                 - Component
## 5                      extracellular region                 - Component
## 6                       extracellular space          16502470 Component

We use parquet for the serialization because it can foster cloud-oriented methods for annotation servicing. With this approach, tidyverse methods are immediately applicable; this is not so for the AnnotationDbi approach.

In this approach, we do not need separate environments for GO and GO2EG. Similarly, separate environments for mapping REFSEQ, REFSEQ2EG, SYMBOL, SYMBOL2EG are not required. We provide them to prevent legacy code from breaking, but we will not provide them indefinitely.

Creating the parquet

NCBI frequently updates mapping tables in text format. The key URL as of March 2026 is

https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/DATA/

We have

gene2ensembl.gz                 2026-03-12 20:18  277M

gene2refseq.gz                  2026-03-12 20:23  2.0G  
...

The following code operates on the gene2ensembl.gz (after downloading) to create a data resource for all model orgnisms:

library(DBI)
library(duckdb)

con = dbConnect(duckdb())

dbExecute(con, "
  CREATE TABLE gene2ensembl AS
  SELECT *
  FROM read_csv_auto(
    'gene2ensembl.gz',
    delim = '\t',
    header = true,
    compression = 'gzip',
    ignore_errors=TRUE
  )
")

dbExecute(con, "COPY (FROM gene2ensembl) TO 'gene2ensembl.parquet' 
       (FORMAT parquet, COMPRESSION zstd, COMPRESSION_LEVEL 15)")

Creating the extract for human 

library(arrow)
ens = read_parquet("gene2ensembl.parquet")
library(dplyr)
ens |> filter(`#tax_id`==9606L) |> 
  write_parquet(sink="Hs.gene2ensembl.parquet", 
  compression="zstd", compression_level=10L)

This is then placed in the extdata folder for an org.Hs.eg.db-like package.

Creating the environments to support legacy usage

For the task of the creation of a map that has the form of a named list of character vectors, we have

simpleEnvBuilder = function(keys, values, keycolname, valcolname) {
      force(keys)  # this is crucial to avoid delayed evaluation until active binding is triggered
      force(values)
      force(keycolname)
      force(valcolname)
     function(pkgname, target_env_name = "org.Hs.egENSEMBL") {
  stopifnot(is.character(keys))
  stopifnot(is.list(values))
  CURRENT = target_env_name
  CURE = paste0(target_env_name, "_env")
  ns = getNamespace(pkgname)
  assign(CURE, new.env(hash=TRUE), envir=ns)
  nn = lapply(seq_len(length(keys)), function(i) assign(keys[i], values[[i]], envir=get(CURE, envir=ns)))
  f = function() {
    tmp = get(CURE, envir=ns)
    class(tmp) = c("hsParqEnv", "environment")
    attr(tmp, "keycolname") = keycolname
    attr(tmp, "valcolname") = valcolname
    tmp
    }
  rm(list=CURRENT, envir=ns)
  makeActiveBinding(CURRENT, f, ns)
 }
}

This produces environments that function like those of the AnnotationDbi packages.

Omitted environments

The full set of environments offered by the org.Hs.eg.db in Bioc 3.22 is

 [7] "org.Hs.egACCNUM"          "org.Hs.egACCNUM2EG"       "org.Hs.egALIAS2EG"       
[10] "org.Hs.egCHR"             "org.Hs.egCHRLENGTHS"      "org.Hs.egCHRLOC"         
[13] "org.Hs.egCHRLOCEND"       "org.Hs.egENSEMBL"         "org.Hs.egENSEMBL2EG"

[31] "org.Hs.egOMIM2EG"         "org.Hs.egORGANISM"        "org.Hs.egPATH"           
[34] "org.Hs.egPATH2EG"         "org.Hs.egPFAM"            "org.Hs.egPMID"           
[37] "org.Hs.egPMID2EG"         "org.Hs.egPROSITE"         "org.Hs.egREFSEQ"

[43] "org.Hs.egUCSCKG"          "org.Hs.egUNIPROT"
  • the ACCNUM environments refer to Genbank and are not updated by NCBI; they are omitted in 3.23
  • the CHR* environments should not be retrieved from this package and are omitted
  • the `ENZYME and PATH environments refer to old versions of KEGG and are omitted
